_comment: Ceilings and tolerances for tests/perf/gate.py. A metric fails when it is
over its platform's ceiling, when it is significantly slower than the base
commit at `alpha`, or when it is slower by more than `large_change`.
The ceilings are a backstop for a catastrophic regression on hardware the
base was not built on (a main push, a manual run); the comparison with the
base is what catches smaller ones. They are set at about three times the
slowest medians measured on GitHub's Linux runners, which vary a lot
between instances (startup 15-39 ms CPU, 22 MB peak; 1.5-3.4 ms CPU per
request, 26 MB peak). A slower runner or a noisy day must not fail a pull
request; the base commit, measured on the same runner, catches real drift.
The gate prints a note when a metric crosses 60% of its ceiling: tighten
it then, from the numbers in the run's report.
reps: startup runs are cheap and noisy, so there are more of them; the
turn workload is a whole session each. warmup runs are discarded.
tolerance: below this change a metric is never called a regression.
alpha: the one-sided Mann-Whitney U test on the two sample sets.
large_change: fails even without a significant p-value.
